chapter_title: Lab: Small-Scale Filter Pipeline and Ablation Memo
course_outline_concepts: Implement a minimal CCNet-style pipeline on a 10GB CommonCrawl slice: lang-ID -> perplexity filter -> exact dedup -> MinHash near-dedup
Train two small (~125M) models with and without each filter, run a small eval suite
Decontaminate against your eval suite; measure how many false positives the n-gram rule produces
Write ablation-memo.md: one table per filter, one paragraph per observation, explicit hypothesis for anything unexpected
Artifact: reproducible pipeline + memo + two trained checkpoints + eval report
Resource-constrained path: 1GB CommonCrawl slice instead of 10GB; train 50M models instead of 125M; use a smaller eval suite (HellaSwag + LAMBADA).

sources.what_to_extract: Canonical stage order: text extraction -> language ID (fastText) -> exact dedup -> quality scoring by perplexity vs Wikipedia-tuned LM -> shard export. Quality scoring as similarity-to-clean-anchor; this is the pattern the lab reimplements end-to-end.
Heuristic web-cleaning baseline: line-length, bad-word lists, boilerplate removal, English-only filter, deduplication. Serves as the minimum 'no-classifier' filter the lab compares against.

Filter-cascade order (URL -> doc-dedup -> lang -> quality -> content -> para-dedup) with per-stage ablation table; streaming per-document 'attribute' pattern; paragraph-dedup deliberately last because earlier stages change the surviving distribution.

Ablation-table methodology: train small (~1.8B) models for ~30B tokens on each filter variant, compare on fixed eval suite. Per-snapshot vs global MinHash finding. FineWeb-Edu classifier F1 = 82% at threshold >=3. Classifier-based filtering replacing heuristic stacks.

ExactSubstr via suffix array at >=50 tokens; NearDup MinHash with 9000 signatures, b=20 bands x r=450 rows, Jaccard >=0.8; 4.6% LM1B val/train overlap; 3.2% C4 val/train overlap; n-gram decontamination false-positive rate question.
Shingle -> MinHash signature -> LSH banding primitives; banding equation P(collision) = 1 - (1 - s^r)^b used to pick bands-and-rows for a target similarity threshold.
Effective sample size framing: two corpora of equal token count can sit on different scaling curves. Gives a formal lens on why a filter with the same token output can produce a different loss slope.

Be-a-scientist ablation discipline: predict outcome before running, overfit a single batch first, 'random search > grid', 'review the 10 worst examples', and the leaky-abstraction framing that forces one-change-at-a-time comparisons.
